text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today as oil prices held steady but geopolitical risk loomed over the refining sector. The stock is down about 1.2% over two weeks, even as U.S. refineries run at 94% capacity and crude inventories remain relatively lean at 711 million barrels. Today's real trigger appears to be reporting on a potential diesel export ban — a measure that could reshape refiner margins by forcing domestic product gluts and pricing pressure, directly hitting companies like this one that depend on selling refined fuel at profitable spreads.

The broader backdrop adds uncertainty: escalating U.S.–Iran tensions and talk of renewed military action after the midterms create volatility in global oil supply and pricing, while the potential export ban itself carries conflicting signals. If imposed, it could backfire by raising global diesel costs and forcing refiners to lower prices domestically — squeezing the margin refiners earn between buying crude and selling finished fuel.
